title: Cisco Releases Quantum Network Controller and Network-Aware Compiler v0.2.0 for Distributed Quantum Infrastructure - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Cisco's Outshift division released two research prototypes, a Quantum Network Controller exposing Entanglement-as-a-Service and Network-Aware Quantum Compiler v0.2.0 with distributed QEC modeling, positioning Cisco in the control plane for multi-vendor quantum networks.

insights.claim: Cisco Outshift released the Quantum Network Controller, a software-defined control plane that provides an Entanglement-as-a-Service abstraction so compilers, apps and security protocols can request entanglement across multi-vendor QPU hardware without configuring optical paths or timing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Cisco is aiming for the vendor-neutral orchestration layer of quantum networking, mirroring its classical networking position.

insights.claim: The controller has a northbound declarative-intent API exposing rate, fidelity and timing requests, a stateful protocol engine and scheduler that handles swapping, teleportation, auto-retry and idle link reclamation, and a hardware abstraction layer normalizing multi-vendor devices including Qunnect and Swabian Instruments.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Southbound adapters for third-party hardware are the key to ecosystem lock-in.

insights.claim: Because quantum states cannot be inspected without collapse, the controller uses closed-loop statistical telemetry to monitor link health and trigger tuning or re-initialization when performance degrades.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Classical network monitoring does not transfer directly; statistical telemetry is a necessary new design pattern.
insights.locator: Because quantum states cannot be inspected

insights.claim: In a prior deployment across 17.6 kilometers of commercial telecom fiber in New York City, the software stack achieved polarization fidelity above 99% at room temperature using third-party hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A metro-fiber demonstration with third-party hardware supports the interoperability claim.

insights.claim: Compiler v0.2.0 integrates circuit compilation, qubit partitioning and distributed QEC against physical network parameters such as optical switch delay, fiber attenuation, communication-qubit constraints and inter-QPU surface code lattice surgery.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Compilation that accounts for network loss is a prerequisite for scaling beyond one QPU module.
insights.locator: The Network-Aware Quantum Compiler v0.2.0 integrates

insights.claim: Capacity-constrained partitioning uses graph-cut strategies Kernighan-Lin, METIS and temporal window-based partitioning to keep heavily interacting qubits on the same QPU and minimize remote gates.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Borrowing classical graph partitioners shows how much of the stack reuses known algorithms.

insights.claim: A Total Logical Error Rate (TLER) metric combines local gate errors, network Bell-pair decay, memory idling and magic state factories to let architects compare network topologies and code distances before physical execution.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A single simulation metric helps design distributed fault-tolerant systems pre-hardware.

insights.claim: Both products are described as research prototypes, and Cisco offers a free 30-day demo of the compiler.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Prototype status with a free demo suggests developer-ecosystem seeding, not revenue.
